videoTitle: The Chinese Paddlefish: The River Giant We Lost
description:
A giant fish once moved through China's longest river. The Chinese paddlefish had a long paddle-shaped snout, a powerful body, and a life built around one great river journey.

This documentary follows the fish through deep water, feeding grounds, long trips upstream, heavy fishing, a dam that cut off its route, the last confirmed sighting in twenty-oh-three, and the searches that found nothing.

intro.title: The Chinese Paddlefish
intro.subtitle: The river giant we lost
intro.hookText: The last signal vanished in hours.
intro.narration: In early twenty-oh-three, a giant fish was pulled from China's longest river. It was treated, tagged, and released alive. Within hours, its signal was gone. No one ever confirmed another living Chinese paddlefish. A creature built for one of the world's great rivers had slipped out of history.

scenes.title: One River, One Home
scenes.subtitle: China's longest river
scenes.narration: The Chinese paddlefish lived in China's longest river and the waters near its mouth. The river gave it deep channels, rich feeding grounds, and a path far inland. Adults moved through a world of brown current and shifting sand. Young fish grew as they travelled toward wider water. Every part of their lives depended on a river that stayed connected.

scenes.title: Built Like No Other Fish
scenes.subtitle: A long paddle-shaped snout
scenes.narration: Its shape was hard to mistake. A long flat snout stretched far ahead of the head. Behind it came a smooth pale body, small eyes, and a strong forked tail. Reliable records show that some reached about three metres, and larger claims remain uncertain. Even at a safe estimate, this was one of the great fish of its river.

scenes.title: A Hunter in Deep Water
scenes.subtitle: Following fish below the surface
scenes.narration: This paddlefish did not strain tiny food from the water. It hunted other fish. Its long snout helped it notice movement in dark and muddy places. The large mouth could take prey while the body kept moving through the current. In the deep river, its strange face was part of a working hunting tool.

scenes.title: The Long River Journey
scenes.subtitle: Upstream to lay eggs
scenes.narration: Adult paddlefish could not stay in one stretch of water. When the time came to breed, they moved far upstream. There, fast water and gravel gave their eggs a place to begin. The young then travelled back toward the middle and lower river. This long round trip had worked for many generations.

scenes.title: Part of a Living River
scenes.subtitle: One link in a wide food web
scenes.narration: The giant fish shared the river with hundreds of other kinds of fish. It ate some, while its own eggs and young fed other animals. Its journeys linked distant parts of the same waterway. People also knew it as a valuable catch. The paddlefish belonged to both the natural life of the river and the lives built along its banks.

scenes.title: Nets Closed In
scenes.subtitle: Heavy fishing in the nineteen seventies
scenes.narration: For years, the fish was taken for food. In the nineteen seventies, the yearly catch was still measured in tens of tons. Large adults were especially costly to lose because the group replaced them slowly. Even after direct fishing stopped, paddlefish were still caught by nets meant for other fish. By the time strong protection arrived, the fall was already well under way.

scenes.title: A Wall Across the River
scenes.subtitle: The route closed in nineteen eighty-one
scenes.narration: Then the river itself was cut in two. In nineteen eighty-one, a large dam closed across the paddlefish's route. Adults below it could no longer reach old breeding water upstream. There was no way around the wall for a fish built to make that journey. Fishing had reduced the numbers, and the blocked river made recovery far harder.

scenes.title: The Last Signal
scenes.subtitle: The final confirmed sighting
scenes.narration: By the nineteen nineties, sightings were rare. Then, in early twenty-oh-three, a living paddlefish was caught by accident. A team cared for the injured fish and returned it to the river with a tracking tag. The signal disappeared within hours. That release became the last confirmed sighting of the species.

scenes.title: The Search Found Nothing
scenes.subtitle: Years without a confirmed fish
scenes.narration: Search teams returned to the river again and again. They used nets, listening gear, market checks, and reports from local fishers. No confirmed Chinese paddlefish appeared. A wide search in twenty seventeen and twenty eighteen recorded hundreds of other kinds of fish, but not this one. The silence was no longer a gap between sightings. It was evidence of a final loss.

scenes.title: A Warning That Came Too Late
scenes.subtitle: Protect the route, not only the animal
scenes.narration: Researchers place the final loss between twenty-oh-five and twenty ten. In twenty twenty-two, the world's main wildlife status list confirmed the Chinese paddlefish was extinct. Protection had focused on the animal after too few were left. Its story shows that a travelling fish also needs a free path, safe breeding water, and time to recover. Saving a river species means keeping its whole journey alive.

outro.title: Keep the Whole Journey Alive
outro.subtitle: Action must come before the last sighting
outro.hookText: A river route can be as vital as water.
outro.narration: The Chinese paddlefish did not vanish in one day. Nets reduced it, a dam blocked it, and action came after the last chance had nearly passed.
